docRequirement: Hook input must carry a common `effort` field — an object with a `level` field holding the turn's active effort level (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"`, `"max"`), downgraded to the level the model actually used when the requested level exceeds model support — present on events that fire within a tool-use context, named as `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop` and `SubagentStop`. The same level must also be readable as the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable by hook commands AND by Bash tool commands. (whats-new/2026-w19.md:47: "Hooks now receive the active effort level via the `effort.level` JSON input field and the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable, and Bash tool commands can read $CLAUDE_EFFORT"; corroborated on the canonical contract page, the `effort` row of hooks.md § Common input fields, line 637 in a 2026-08-03 fetch: "Object with a `level` field holding the active effort level for the turn … The level is also available to hook commands and the Bash tool as the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable.")
current:
Nothing supplies the level to either surface, although the host holds it.

Hook JSON input: `SdkAutomationInput` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742-902) has no `effort` member of any spelling and no index signature, and `hookCommandStdinPayload` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-651) serialises exactly that object — `{...input, hook_event_name, cwd?}` — adding nothing. Both hook execution authorities use that payload: the direct spawn at hook-command.ts:653/664 and the host's sandboxed runner at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488.

Hook env: `buildHookCommandEnv` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:46-81) emits `NESSY_EVENT`, `NESSY_EVENT_DATA`, the six `SAFE_INHERITED_ENV_KEYS` (hook-command.ts:34 — HOME/PATH/SHELL/TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP) and fourteen `NESSY_*` payload mirrors (:61-74), then the action's own `env` (:76-78). No effort key in either spelling. SessionManager.ts:4344 calls that same builder and passes its result at :4490 (`env: { ...env, ...runner.environment }`), so both authorities are covered by the one absence. The exec-form placeholder list (hook-command.ts:161-170) is a closed list of eight path placeholders with no EFFORT entry.

Bash tool env: the runtime-backed `bash` tool (packages/pi-agent-server/src/local-tools/runtime-backed-tools.ts:252-258, :353-354) routes to the host, whose `handleProcessStartRequest` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:5138-5214) rebuilds the supervisor request from an allowlist and composes the only host-added env at :5191-5200 — plugin `PLUGIN_ROOT`/`PLUGIN_DATA` variants plus `PATH`. The supervisor then merges `hostEnvironment(profile)` (filtered by `RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT`, packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:703-714) with `...request.env` at :174-176. No effort variable enters at any of those points, so `echo $CLAUDE_EFFORT` in a Bash call prints an empty line. The Pi subprocess env itself (pi-agent.ts:1462-1477) likewise carries only proxy vars, `envOverrides`, AWS vars, `NESSY_SESSION_DIR`, `NESSY_SESSION_ID`, `NESSY_DEBUG`.

The value exists and is reachable at every one of those points: `BaseAgent._thinkingLevel` (base-agent.ts:297, :473) with the public `getThinkingLevel()`/`getModel()` accessors (base-agent.ts:1537-1552, declared on `AgentBackend` at packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:1005 and :1033), the documented vocabulary map `THINKING_TO_EFFORT` (packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts:70-77), the model downgrade rule `clampThinkingLevelToModel` (thinking-levels.ts:236-247) and `resolveEffortLevel` (thinking-levels.ts:200-206). The skill subsystem already consumes it: `runtimeSkillHostContext` (base-agent.ts:2200-2207) passes `effort: this._thinkingLevel` and `SKILL_VARIABLE_SPELLINGS` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:136) maps it to `['NESSY_EFFORT','CLAUDE_EFFORT']` — but that is markdown text substitution in a skill body, never a process environment variable, so no hook and no shell can read it.
divergence: Pure absence on two surfaces, not a wrong value or a misspelled key. The level itself is correct and already computed host-side in the documented vocabulary; it is simply never written into (a) the hook input object, (b) the hook command environment, (c) the Bash/child-process environment. Two details a fix must get right rather than guess: the input field is an OBJECT — `effort: { level: … }` — not a bare `effort: string`, and `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` is the documented spelling on both env surfaces even though this fork's convention is `NESSY_*` (the skill path already ships both spellings, so the precedent is to emit both, not to rename). Nessy also has a sixth level, `off`, which is not in the documented five; the skill path withholds the variable for `off` (base-agent.ts:2205) and the hook/Bash surfaces should do the same rather than emit a word the docs do not list.

change.what: Add one optional member to the interface (currently :742-902), beside the other tool-context fields: `effort?: { level: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max' }`. Object, not a bare string — hooks.md § Common input fields spells it "Object with a `level` field". Comment it with the verbatim sentence and the presence rule (tool-use-context events; the downgraded level when the model narrows it; `xhigh` is what Ultracode reports as). Do NOT reuse `ThinkingLevel` for the literal union: that type includes Nessy's `off`, which is not a documented level.

One injection point covers every event. Inside the wrapped `executeAgentEvent` (:5382-5388), before the `enqueueAgentAutomationEvent(...)` call, derive the level from the session's own agent and merge it into `input`: `const level = managed.agent ? clampThinkingLevelToModel(managed.agent.getThinkingLevel(), managed.agent.getModel()) : undefined` and pass `{ ...input, ...(level && level !== 'off' && EFFORT_INPUT_EVENTS.has(event) ? { effort: { level } } : {}) }`. Add a module-local `const EFFORT_INPUT_EVENTS: ReadonlySet<AgentEvent> = new Set(['PreToolUse', 'PostToolUse', 'Stop', 'SubagentStop'])` — the four the page names; extend to the fork's tool-context siblings (`PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`) only as a deliberate, commented superset, since "such as" makes the list non-exhaustive. Import `clampThinkingLevelToModel` from `@nessy-agent/shared` (packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts). This wrapper is the single funnel: `managed.agent?.setAutomationSystem(agentAutomationSystem)` at :11512 hands the SAME wrapper to the agent, so `BaseAgent.emitAutomationEvent` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:1438-1457) → `dispatchAutomationAgentEvent` (packages/shared/src/automations/lifecycle-hook-dispatcher.ts:24) lands here, and so do the host-emitted events that bypass the agent entirely — `SubagentStop` at :5764, the child-terminal sites at :5596 and :5636, and :10512. Injecting in `BaseAgent.emitAutomationEvent` instead is the tempting one-liner and it is wrong: it does not reach `SubagentStop`, which the page names explicitly and which SessionManager emits directly.

Two lines after the existing `setSanitized` block (:61-74): `setSanitized(env, 'NESSY_EFFORT', input.effort?.level);` and `setSanitized(env, 'CLAUDE_EFFORT', input.effort?.level);`. Both spellings, mirroring `SKILL_VARIABLE_SPELLINGS` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:136) and the dual plugin-env spelling — an imported Claude plugin's hook script reads `$CLAUDE_EFFORT`. `setSanitized` already no-ops on `undefined`, so absence needs no guard, and placing it before the `actionEnv` loop (:76-78) keeps a hook's own `env` able to override. This one edit serves both execution authorities: the direct spawn (:664) and SessionManager's sandboxed runner (:4344 → :4490).

Extend the host-composed env at :5191-5200 (currently named `pluginEnvironment`; rename to `childEnvironment` since it stops being plugin-only) with the effort variables: compute `const level = clampThinkingLevelToModel(this._thinkingLevel, this._model)` and spread `...(level === 'off' ? {} : { NESSY_EFFORT: level, CLAUDE_EFFORT: level })`. This is the host's allowlist rebuild for every child-requested process start, so it reaches the Bash tool (runtime-backed `bash` → packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1565 `runCommand` → `requestSupervisedProcess`) and its grep/find/ls siblings. No change is needed in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts: `...request.env` is merged over the profile-filtered host env at :174-176, so `RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT` (:703-711) does not have to list the key. Read the level at request time, not at spawn time — `setThinkingLevel` (base-agent.ts:1549) can change it mid-session while the subprocess lives on, which is exactly why the init-message `thinkingLevel` (pi-agent.ts:1531) is not a usable source here.

Second Bash surface, needed only for full coverage. `runDefaultCommand` (:505-539) calls `Bun.spawn(['bash','-lc',command], { cwd, stdout, stderr, signal })` with no `env`, and it is the fallback whenever no `runCommand` is injected (:335). The Nestor Cloud backend takes that fallback: packages/shared/src/agent/nestor-cloud-agent.ts:91-130 constructs `NestorCloudToolExecutor` without `runCommand`, and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/nestor-cloud/tool-executor.ts:107 forwards the `undefined` through. Either add an optional `env` to the `runCommand` options type (packages/shared/src/agent/local-tools/types.ts:107) and thread it into `Bun.spawn`, or give the Nestor Cloud executor a supervisor-backed `runCommand` like Pi's. Skip only if the owner scopes this row to the Pi default backend — say so in the tracker rather than leaving it silent.

Exact-shape assertions break once `effort` rides the input. :357-364 does `expect(stop?.input).toEqual({ hook_event_name: 'Stop', stop_hook_active: false, background_tasks: [], session_crons: [] })`. Update this and the sibling `toEqual` input assertions in packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/codex-agent-lifecycle-hooks.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-defer.test.ts and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/permission-events-composed.test.ts. Note these agent-level suites assert what the AGENT emits, which is upstream of the SessionManager wrapper — if injection lands only in the wrapper, they may need no change at all; run them before editing rather than pre-emptively rewriting expectations.

Two new cases, one positive one negative: `buildHookCommandEnv` with `input.effort = { level: 'xhigh' }` sets BOTH `NESSY_EFFORT` and `CLAUDE_EFFORT` to `xhigh`; with `effort` absent it sets neither key. Add a matching pair for the wrapper (`effort` present on a `PreToolUse`/`SubagentStop` input, absent on a `SessionStart` input, absent when the level is `off`) in a server-core test beside the existing hook-event suites.

blastRadius:
Crosses a process boundary and a persistence boundary — both risk triggers in this repo.

- Hook stdin JSON and `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` are an EXTERNAL contract: third-party `command` hooks and imported Claude/Codex plugin hook scripts parse them. The change is purely additive (a new optional key), so it cannot break a reader, but it is still a change to what leaves the host.
- `SdkAutomationInput` has ~62 referencing sites across packages/shared/src/automations, packages/shared/src/plugins, packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts and packages/pi-agent-server/src/compat/pi-runtime-adapter.ts. Adding an optional member is source-compatible; nothing iterates the object generically except `hookCommandStdinPayload` (:641) and `JSON.stringify(input)` in `buildHookCommandEnv` (:53), both of which want the new field.
- `buildBaseEventEnv` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:392-425) is NOT on this path — it serves prompt/webhook automation actions over `BaseEventPayload` and snake-cases payload keys. Leave it alone; the phase-2 evidence cited it by mistake.
- Bash-side: the added env keys enter `processEnvironment` in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:173-179 and therefore change `environmentDigest` (:734) on every execution receipt. Any recorded receipt fixture or digest-comparing test will shift, and the digest is persisted with the process record (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-store.ts). That is the persistence boundary.
- Downstream hook consumers that will now see the field without further work: packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts (:562 composite, :1646 forwards `input` verbatim to plugin runners), so plugin `http`/`mcp_tool`/`prompt`/`agent` hooks get it too.
- NOT covered by the wrapper injection: the Claude backend's `buildSdkHooks` path (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts, wrapped at SessionManager.ts:5391-5400 without touching input). That backend is off by default (`NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE`) and the Anthropic Agent SDK is the author of its hook input there.
- Tests named in the change list; `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/effort-precedence.test.ts` already covers `resolveEffortLevel`/`clampThinkingLevelToModel` and should stay green untouched.
userImpact: Latent-but-reachable, and silent when it bites. Today: install any Claude plugin whose `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`Stop`/`SubagentStop` hook branches on effort — the common shape is `level=$(jq -r '.effort.level')` or `[ "$CLAUDE_EFFORT" = low ]` to skip an expensive check on cheap turns — and the hook reads `null`/empty and takes the wrong branch. It exits 0, so nothing is logged, no hook-error notice appears in the session, and the user sees only that the plugin "does not seem to do anything": an expensive gate that was meant to be skipped runs on every turn, or a guard that was meant to fire never does. Same for a Bash tool call inside a turn: `echo $CLAUDE_EFFORT` prints a blank line. The asymmetry makes it more surprising, not less — the same documented variable DOES expand inside a skill body (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:136), so a user who verified it in a skill will reasonably assume it works in the hook and the shell too. Nothing surfaces it except reading the hook's own output; no first-party Nessy surface depends on it.
